text: Production data engineering recap — and this course's finale. Three chapters, one throughline: structure, then motion, then survival.

Chapter one was structure — what fabric even is. OneLake, lakehouses, warehouses, notebooks, direct lake, semantic models, capacities, and git integration — mapped explicitly back to databricks and delta lake at nearly every step.

Chapter two was motion — data that never stops arriving. Eventstreams, KQL databases, the full KQL language, three window shapes, watermarks, activator, streamed CDC — all the way to lesson forty-one's full capstone pipeline.

Chapter three was survival. CI/CD, testing, contracts, observability, cost, SLAs, incident response, root cause analysis, on-call — closing in lesson sixty-nine with every piece working together in one real incident.

Three courses down in this data engineering track, with a career and capstone course still ahead when you're ready for it. Every cross-reference back to databricks throughout this course was never a coincidence — it was always one continuous story.
